wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.protocol_origin: A copy of KDE's server-decoration.xml, kept in the wayland-rs repository. The LGPL text comes from https://github.com/KDE/plasma-wayland-protocols/tree/3d8327f5c8727702c5b14730c32d70b30e2ae106.
wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.used_by: smithay-client-toolkit 0.20.0, through smithay-clipboard, uses only the input-method protocol from this crate.
wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.license_text_note: The crate ships only its MIT LICENSE.txt, so licenses/rust/manifest.json supplies the LGPL text from the KDE commit above.

wayland-protocols-plasma@0.3.12.used_by: winit 0.30.13 always enables this crate with its wayland feature, for KDE blur only. ReShiki never requests blur.

facts: Both crates declare MIT, but wayland-scanner generates their Rust code at build time from the KDE protocol descriptions listed above, which are LGPL-2.1-or-later. The other bundled descriptions are MIT-CMU, MIT or BSD-3-Clause, or carry no licence header (fullscreen-shell.xml). Both crates are Linux-only dependencies of ReShiki.
binary_content: The generated code holds interface, request, event and argument names, signatures and version numbers. Descriptions become doc comments, which compilation drops. A Linux release build on Ubuntu arm64 with these versions contains org_kde_* interface names, but no description text and no copyright or SPDX lines.
reason: Only interface identifiers and message layouts reach the binary. LGPL-2.1 section 5 leaves object code unrestricted when it uses only numerical parameters, data structure layouts and accessors, and small macros and small inline functions from the library's header material. The complete LGPL-2.1 text ships in the third-party notices together with this record. ReShiki's complete source, Cargo.lock and build instructions are public, so a recipient can modify these crates and rebuild. ReShiki keeps the KDE notices and does not relicense the protocol descriptions.
review: This record covers only the package versions, checksums and file digests above. license_notices.py fails when either crate has an unreviewed version or its bundled GPL-family protocol files change. check_agent_dependencies.py fails when Cargo.lock moves either crate away from the reviewed version and checksum.
